title: On the Moon, a Hammer and a Feather Hit the Ground Together

scenes.text: On the Moon, a hammer and a feather hit the ground at the same time.
Apollo 15 commander David Scott did it live, on his last moonwalk.
He held a three-pound hammer and a falcon feather at shoulder height.
He let go. Both landed together.
The Moon has almost no air, so nothing slows the feather.
A hammer and a feather. Same time.

description:
On the last Apollo 15 moonwalk in 1971, commander David Scott dropped a hammer and a falcon feather at the same time. They hit the surface together.
The Moon has almost no atmosphere, so there is no air resistance to slow the feather. It confirmed an idea Galileo had reasoned centuries earlier.
What else would you drop on the Moon? Tell us.
first_comment: The feather is still on the Moon today. What would you leave up there?
